nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Only a small fraction of light reaches the dim forest floor, so canopy trees capture most of the energy that enters the web.

nodes.name: Monsoon rainfall
nodes.desc: Heavy seasonal rain keeps the lowland forest wet year round and feeds the rivers that cross the reserve.

nodes.name: Forest soil and litter
nodes.desc: Leaf litter and nutrient-poor tropical soil, recycled quickly by decomposers, supply the trees.

nodes.name: Mineral licks
nodes.desc: Natural mineral-rich spots that forest ungulates, elephants and tapirs visit to supplement their diet.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen wood, leaves and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Dipterocarp trees
nodes.desc: Tall emergent and canopy trees that dominate lowland rainforest in Peninsular Malaysia and shape the structure of the forest.

nodes.name: Fig trees
nodes.desc: Figs fruit heavily and are an important food for many forest birds and mammals.

nodes.name: Baccaurea trees
nodes.desc: Understory fruit tree recorded in the reserve; its fruit is eaten by macaques and mouse-deer according to GloBI records.

nodes.name: Ebony relatives
nodes.desc: Understory tree of the ebony genus recorded in the reserve; its fruit is eaten by mouse-deer in GloBI records.

nodes.name: Asian elephant
nodes.desc: Largest land animal of the reserve; a wide-ranging browser and grazer that opens paths and moves through the forest.

nodes.name: Gaur (seladang)
nodes.desc: Massive wild ox of Peninsular Malaysia that eats grasses and browse and is a main prey of the Malayan tiger.

nodes.name: Malayan tapir
nodes.desc: Solitary herbivore that eats shoots and leaves from over a hundred plant species; recorded repeatedly in the reserve.

nodes.name: Indian muntjac
nodes.desc: Small forest deer that eats leaves, fruit and shoots; prey of tigers and other large predators.

nodes.name: Lesser mouse-deer
nodes.desc: Tiny hoofed mammal of the forest floor that eats fallen fruit and leaves.

nodes.name: Long-tailed macaque
nodes.desc: Omnivorous monkey that eats fruit, seeds and small animals.

nodes.name: Dusky leaf monkey
nodes.desc: Tree-living monkey that eats mainly leaves, along with fruit and flowers.

nodes.name: Rhinoceros hornbill
nodes.desc: Large forest bird whose diet is dominated by fruit, including figs, plus some insects and small animals.

nodes.name: Fungus-growing termites
nodes.desc: Termites that gather dead plant matter and recycle it; a food source for frogs and other small animals.

nodes.name: Leopard cat
nodes.desc: Small wild cat that hunts small mammals; GloBI records include dusky leaf monkey and plantain squirrel.

nodes.name: Clouded monitor
nodes.desc: Common large lizard of the forest that eats frogs and other small animals.

nodes.name: Water monitor
nodes.desc: Big lizard near streams that hunts amphibians and also feeds on carrion.

nodes.name: Banded bullfrog
nodes.desc: Burrowing frog that eats ants, termites and other small insects.

nodes.name: Malayan tiger
nodes.desc: Top predator of the reserve; it takes large hoofed prey, including barking deer (muntjac) and wild cattle such as gaur.
